items.title: milume
items.text:
Explore spatial biology in your notebook.

Layer images, cells, and transcripts in 3D, in one reactive widget.

import milume

w = milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type")

items.title: Data model and coordinates
items.text: Why milume reads AnnData and SpatialData the way it does, which coordinate frame everything shares, and what crosses between Python and the widget.

items.title: AnnData is the analysis object
items.text: milume draws the AnnData you already have. Cell positions come from obsm["spatial"] (or another key you name with spatial_key), labels come from obs columns, and expression comes from X. The widget holds a reference to your AnnData. It doesn't copy obs and it doesn't make a dense copy of X, so the map always shows the object your code works on.

items.title: What milume takes from SpatialData
items.text: A SpatialData object adds images and cell shapes. When you pass one to milume.peek, milume picks a table: the only table, or the one whose region links a labels element. Otherwise you name it with table=. The table's coordinates draw the 2D map. If the object holds exactly one 3D image and is backed by a Zarr store on disk, the widget can also open the Inspect cube. The cube's cells come from a shapes element with one polygon per cell per z plane, marked by cell_id and Z_um columns. When milume can't use an element, it warns and leaves it out, so the map still opens.

items.title: One coordinate frame
items.text:
The map, selections, landmarks and the Inspect window all use the units of the table's coordinates: micrometres for Pyxa and Xenium, pixels for CosMx. milume doesn't reproject anything. The cube takes its frame from the image's transform into the shapes' coordinate system (global when it exists) and supports only scale plus translation, so a window position and obsm["spatial"] mean the same place. CosMx stores FOV-local pixels in obsm["spatial"], which is why the loading guide passes spatial_key="global".

milume reads the unit from reader or NGFF metadata and falls back to cell spacing when there is none. It uses the unit only to size default raster bins.

items.title: What Python sees: synced state
items.text: Only a few named values cross between Python and the browser after the widget opens: selections, landmarks, the focused selection, and the Inspect window (inspect_cx, inspect_cy, inspect_open, volume_cut). A selection is an analysis region. You read its cells as obs_names with get_obs_names, never as row positions, so the result survives subsetting and reordering. A landmark is a durable annotation in the same coordinates, and it round-trips through a GeoDataFrame. In marimo, wrap the widget in mo.ui.anywidget so cells that read these values re-run when they change.

items.title: Design principles
items.text: The choices behind milume ("visualize, don't compute"), so you know what to expect from the widget and what stays in your own code.

items.title: Explore spatial biology in your notebook
items.text: milume puts a tissue map in a notebook cell so you can look, select and carry what you selected back into code. These principles explain how it does that and where it stops.

items.title: Python owns analysis, the browser owns presentation
items.text: The widget computes only what it needs to draw and to select: raster bins, neighborhoods, probe scores and color scales. It doesn't normalize, cluster or test anything, and it never writes into your AnnData. Normalization, clustering and statistics stay in your code, with scanpy, squidpy or anything else. The measure helpers (distances, composition, enrichment and the others) run only when you call them and return DataFrames. They write an obs column only when you call write_obs.

items.title: Results are plain data
items.text: Everything you take out of the widget is an ordinary object: obs_names for a selection, a GeoDataFrame for landmarks, and a DataFrame for a measurement. Nothing depends on milume being installed to read it later, and you can hand the same regions to another tool.

items.title: Synced state stays small
items.text: Each widget declares its synced values as named, typed fields instead of one shared blob. A value is synced only when Python reads it, sets it or computes it. Camera, colors, layer toggles and cube settings stay in the widget. Each value has one owner, so a notebook slider and a widget control never fight over it. Controls redraw on every frame while you drag and update Python once when you let go, so dependent cells run once per gesture.

items.title: Nothing to build
items.text: The widget's browser code is compiled ahead of time and shipped in the wheel. pip install milume is all a notebook user needs, with no Node or frontend toolchain. Runtime dependencies are kept small for the same reason.

items.title: Alongside other viewers
items.text: milume is for forming intuition quickly. When you need to look at a dataset in depth, use a dedicated viewer and bring the same selections and landmarks with you.

items.title: How rendering works
items.text: How the 2D map and the Inspect cube draw large data in a notebook: points vs raster, lazy genes, and windowed multiscale image loading under a voxel budget.

items.title: The 2D map: one canvas
items.text:
The map is a single deck.gl canvas in flat, orthographic coordinates. Cells, selections, landmarks, drafts and neighborhood overlays all draw on it, so they can't drift apart when you pan or zoom. Marker size comes from the median distance between neighboring cells. Neighborhood expansion (k-NN or radius) runs in the browser from the coordinates. It needs no neighbor graph from Python.

The 2D map doesn't draw the tissue image or cell outlines yet. Those appear in the Inspect cube.

items.title: Points and raster
items.text: In points mode, each cell is one marker. In raster mode, the browser sorts cells into square bins and gives each bin the mean, or the category mix, of the cells within a window around its centre. In micrometre data, the defaults are 8 µm bins and a 24 µm window. Raster suits dense sections, where points overlap and hide each other. Probe compares bins by similarity. Bins and scores live only in the browser.

items.title: Genes load when you color by them
items.text: At startup only gene names reach the browser. A gene's column is fetched from the kernel the first time you color by it, then kept in a size-limited browser cache that never drops a gene on screen. So a whole-transcriptome panel opens as fast as a small one. genes=[...] preloads a short list instead, up to 64 MiB. For color, each gene is scaled from its minimum to its 99th percentile. That scaling is for display only and doesn't change X.

items.title: The Inspect cube reads one window
items.text: Inspect places a 300 µm square on the map and opens a cube of that window through the full depth of the image. The browser reads only that box from one level of the image pyramid over the widget's own connection, and never reads tables or expression that way. Cells in the window are built into meshes in a Web Worker and colored from the category panel. The cube's Points layer (cell centres) is off by default.

items.title: Choosing an image level: the voxel budget
items.text: The hover preview uses a coarse level. The open cube picks the sharpest level whose window fits 64 Mi voxels (about 64 MB of 8-bit texture) and at most 2,048 voxels per axis. Nothing is hard-coded per dataset. On the 3D demo tier, a full-resolution window is over the budget, so the cube loads the next level.

items.title: Which data sizes this covers
items.text: Demo data runs from tiny test fixtures to a 2D section, a 3D tier and a full colon run. Tier paths, on-disk sizes, and citations are on Datasets.

items.title: pip
items.text:
pip install milume

Requires Python 3.11+.

Each demo notebook lists its own dependencies in its inline script header, so uvx marimo edit --sandbox demos/landmarks.py (or opening it on molab) installs them for you. The Squidpy recipe also needs scanpy, squidpy and leidenalg:

pip install squidpy scanpy leidenalg

items.title: uv
items.text:
uv pip install --compile-bytecode milume

--compile-bytecode compiles .pyc files at install time, so the first import milume doesn't pay for compiling milume and its dependencies. In a project, uv add milume works too (set UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1 for the same effect).

items.title: From source
items.text:
uv sync --group demo --group dev

The demo dependency group adds marimo and the spatial-omics packages used by demos/. It is a development group, not a published extra.

items.title: Tutorial: explore cells in 2D
items.text: Walk through the ileum molab notebook on Xu et al. 2026 ileum MERFISH (#343). Each step below matches one section of the notebook and shows a visible result on the map or in a table.

items.title: 1. Load the ileum slice
items.text:
Download the slice with ml.datasets or the short alias ml.ds (pinned URL, user cache). The matrix X is already the authors' log-normalized values — do not call normalize_total or log1p.

import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()

Result: adata is 30,332 cells × 1,815 genes with obsm["spatial"] in micrometres. The notebook preloads a small curated gene list in ml.peek(..., genes=...) so the widget export stays within the static payload budget. See the Datasets reference for fields and citation.

items.title: 2. Open the map on cell types
items.text:
DEMO_GENES = [
    "Apob", "Slc5a1", "Nos2", "Cps1", "Mki67", "Lgr5", "Erbb3", "H2-Eb1",
    "Acta2", "Col1a1", "Phox2b", "Kit", "Pecam1", "Mzb1", "Cd3e", "Csf1r",
    "Cxcl13", "Cr2", "Ccr7",
]
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type", genes=DEMO_GENES)
w

Result: The full ileum ring appears, coloured by cell_type.

items.title: 3. Layer and villus–crypt genes
items.text:
Recolour in place — no new figure objects:

w.color = "anatomical_layer"  # mucosa, submucosa, muscle, GALT
w.color = "Apob"              # villus-tip enterocytes
w.color = "Cps1"              # crypt / lower villus

Result: You see the crypt–villus axis and the GALT patches in anatomical layers before you select them.

items.title: 4. Lasso GALT cryptopatch aggregates
items.text:
Use the Select tool and lasso each GALT cryptopatch on the map (Select regions). Xu et al. annotate these as small ILF-like aggregates (rich in cDC, ILC3, and FRC), not classical B/T follicles. Each edit updates w.selections.

The notebook seeds two tight polygons (galt-aggregates-west and galt-aggregates-east). Join them for downstream analysis:

galt_hits = w.get_obs_names("galt-aggregates-west").union(
    w.get_obs_names("galt-aggregates-east")
)

Result: The seeded headless lassos select 278 cells in total, 261 with anatomical_layer GALT (93.9% of the selection), covering all 260 annotated GALT cells in the two cryptopatch aggregates on this slice. The western polygon is 90.2% GALT (164 cells, 148 GALT); the tightened eastern polygon is 99.1% GALT (114 cells, 113 GALT). Your own lassos may differ.

items.title: 5. Enrichment and violin plots
items.text:
enrich = ml.enrichment(adata, galt_hits, obs_key="cell_type")
enrich

Result: Stromal and innate immune types rank highest by log2_enrichment relative to the whole section (seeded union: FRC 6.20, cDC (Il22ra2+) 6.04, ILC3 5.66, FDC 5.35, B (follicular) 4.52).

Flag the selection and plot immune markers:

adata.obs["galt_vs_rest"] = "rest"
adata.obs.loc[galt_hits, "galt_vs_rest"] = "GALT selection"
sc.pl.violin(adata, ["Mzb1", "Cd3e"], groupby="galt_vs_rest")

Result: Mzb1 and Cd3e are higher in the GALT selection than in the rest of the section.

items.title: Tutorial: 3D with SpatialData
items.text: Follow the Landmarks molab demo: Pyxa small/ from Hugging Face, clustering for colour, then image + cell outlines → Inspect cube (#339, #343).

items.title: 1. Load the 3D tier
items.text:
Download Stellaromics/demo small/ (transcript CSV omitted in the demo — about 247 MB) and build SpatialData with the Pyxa reader:

from pathlib import Path

from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download
from spatialdata_io.experimental import pyxa

data_dir = (
    Path(
        snapshot_download(
            "Stellaromics/demo",
            repo_type="dataset",
            allow_patterns="small/*",
            ignore_patterns="*cell_assigned_gene*",
        )
    )
    / "small"
)
pyxa_sdata = pyxa(data_dir, cell_assigned_gene=False)

Result: Table with 4,372 cells, DAPI mosaic, and per-z cell outline polygons in micrometres. Details: Datasets.

items.title: 2. Clusters for colour
items.text:
import scanpy as sc

adata = pyxa_sdata.tables["rna"]
sc.pp.log1p(adata)
sc.pp.pca(adata)
sc.pp.neighbors(adata)
sc.tl.leiden(adata, key_added="cluster", flavor="leidenalg", n_iterations=2)
pyxa_sdata.tables["rna"] = adata

Result: A cluster column for milume.peek(..., color="cluster"). The demo uses log1p on counts only — not normalize_total.

items.title: 3. Write Zarr and open the map
items.text:
Inspect reads the image from a SpatialData Zarr store on disk:

import spatialdata as sd
import tempfile

store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="milume-")) / "small.sdata.zarr"
pyxa_sdata.write(store, overwrite=True)
sdata = sd.read_zarr(store)

import milume

w = milume.peek(sdata, color="cluster")
w

Result: Coloured cells on the 2D map over the Pyxa section.

items.title: 4. Inspect: image and cell meshes
items.text:
Click an empty area of the widget so it has keyboard focus, then press I and click the tissue (Inspect in 3D). The DAPI cube opens with cell outline meshes, not points.

Use the cross-section sliders in the Inspect toolbar to move the cut plane. Saved inspect selections appear in the Selections list like lasso regions.

items.title: 5. Enrichment on an Inspect selection
items.text:
After you save an Inspect window, read its cells and run composition:

inspect_id = w.selections[-1]["id"]
hits = w.get_obs_names(inspect_id)
milume.enrichment(adata, hits, obs_key="cluster")

Result: A table of cluster proportions inside the cube window versus the whole dataset.

items.title: 6. Drive Inspect from Python
items.text:
Open or move the cube without a click when the widget already has a 3D volume:

w.inspect_cx, w.inspect_cy = 120.0, 140.0
w.inspect_open = True
w.volume_cut  # read cut state after slider moves

Setting inspect_open = False closes the cube and exits Inspect. See synced traitlets.

items.title: Draw and export landmarks
items.text: Draw landmarks on the map, export them as vector data, and load edits back into the widget.

items.title: Goal
items.text: Move landmarks between milume and GeoPandas (or any tool that reads GeoJSON/Shapefile via GeoDataFrame).

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Open milume on spatial data (ileum demo):
import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w

  1. Draw or edit landmarks in the browser (Landmarks). Each edit updates w.landmarks.

  2. Convert the synced list to a GeoDataFrame (geopandas required):

import geopandas as gpd
from milume import landmarks_to_geodataframe, geodataframe_to_landmarks

gdf = landmarks_to_geodataframe(w.landmarks)
gdf.to_file("landmarks.geojson", driver="GeoJSON")
  1. Edit gdf offline, then push it back:
gdf = gpd.read_file("landmarks.geojson")
w.landmarks = geodataframe_to_landmarks(gdf)
  1. Run measure helpers against the same adata and exported geometry when you need distances or composition (Measure API).

items.title: Result
items.text:
landmarks.geojson (or your chosen path) matches what you drew; assigning back to w.landmarks updates the map.

Column semantics and CRS notes are in GeoDataFrame interchange.

items.title: Load AnnData / SpatialData
items.text: Open milume on AnnData or SpatialData you already have in the notebook.

items.title: Goal
items.text: Show spatial cells (and, for SpatialData, the Inspect cube when a 3D image is available) with milume.peek.

items.title: AnnData
items.text:
1. Load AnnData with coordinates in obsm["spatial"] (for example the ileum demo slice):
import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w
  1. If your matrix uses another obsm key, pass spatial_key= when you call peek.

Result: The Landmarks map opens on the ileum section, colored by cell_type.

Constructor options (color, genes, spatial_key, …) are in the LandmarksWidget API.

items.title: SpatialData
items.text:
Install the platform reader once:

pip install spatialdata-io

Then read with the loader for your platform and pass the object to peek. milume infers the table, cell polygons, and 3D image when they are present. Override with table=, image=, labels=, or shapes= when needed (constructor parameters).

items.title: Pyxa
items.text:
1. Install a spatialdata-io build that includes the Pyxa reader (see the Landmarks molab demo pin if the release you use does not yet ship pyxa).

  2. Read Stellaromics Pyxa output into SpatialData:

from pathlib import Path

import spatialdata as sd
from spatialdata_io.experimental import pyxa

data_dir = Path("/path/to/pyxa/small")  # counts, metadata, DAPI mosaic
sdata = pyxa(data_dir, cell_assigned_gene=False)
  1. To use Inspect on the DAPI mosaic, write the store to disk and reopen it (the cube reads the image from Zarr):
store = Path("/tmp/pyxa.sdata.zarr")
sdata.write(store, overwrite=True)
sdata = sd.read_zarr(store)
  1. Open milume on the table you want to color (for example rna after you add a cluster column):
w = milume.peek(sdata, color="cluster")
w

Result: Pyxa cells and mosaic load; Inspect is available after the Zarr round-trip.

items.title: Xenium
items.text:
1. Point spatialdata_io.xenium at the Xenium *_outs folder (or a subset of its files):
import spatialdata_io as sio
import milume

sdata = sio.xenium("/path/to/xenium_outs", transcripts=False)
w = milume.peek(sdata)
w
  1. Set w.color to any categorical column on the table, or pass color= to peek when you open it.

Result: Xenium cells render in global coordinates from obsm["spatial"] (default spatial_key).

Platform-specific reader flags stay in the spatialdata-io docs.

items.title: CosMx
items.text:
1. Read CosMx flat files with spatialdata_io.cosmx:
import spatialdata_io as sio
import milume

sdata = sio.cosmx("/path/to/cosmx_flat_files", dataset_id="my_run", transcripts=False)
  1. Pass spatial_key="global". CosMx FOV-local pixels live in obsm["spatial"]; milume needs global coordinates:
w = milume.peek(sdata, spatial_key="global")
w

Result: CosMx cells from every FOV share one map in global pixel space.

For Inspect behavior on platforms without per-slice cell meshes, see Inspect in 3D.

items.title: Match plot colors (squidpy)
items.text: Color the Landmarks map from Squidpy niche labels and reuse the same hex colors in Matplotlib or Scanpy plots.

items.title: Goal
items.text: Run Squidpy neighborhood niches on a selection, assign w.color to the niche column Squidpy writes, and read colors back with w.category_colors.

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Install optional analysis packages:
pip install scanpy squidpy leidenalg
  1. Open the ileum slice and draw a region to analyze (or use the whole tissue):
import milume as ml
import squidpy as sq

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w  # draw a selection in the browser, then continue
  1. Build a boolean mask aligned to adata.obs_names for the selection you want:
region = w.selections[-1]["id"]
mask = adata.obs_names.isin(w.get_obs_names(region))
  1. Run Squidpy niches on that mask (neighbors + spatial graph first):
sc.pp.neighbors(adata)
sq.gr.spatial_neighbors_knn(adata, n_neighs=6)
sq.gr.calculate_niche(
    adata,
    flavor="neighborhood",
    groups="cell_type",
    n_neighbors=6,
    resolutions=0.5,
    mask=mask,
)
niche_col = "nhood_niche_res=0.5"
  1. Colour the map from the new column:
w.color = niche_col
  1. Reuse the map palette elsewhere:
palette = w.category_colors(niche_col)  # {label: "#rrggbb"}

items.title: Result
items.text:
Landmarks points and downstream plots share the same label-to-color mapping as the map.

For a prepared studio walkthrough (fixed selection and export state), use the Squidpy niche color recipe or the live molab notebook. The recipe export pipeline is unchanged; this page is the task-only steps.

Squidpy and Scanpy parameters stay in their own docs; milume traitlets are in the LandmarksWidget API.

items.title: Use selections downstream
items.text: Carry lasso, rectangle, and inspect selections into pandas, Scanpy, or other Python analysis.

items.title: Goal
items.text: Turn the cells inside a map selection into an observation subset or a boolean column on adata.obs.

items.title: Steps
items.text:
1. Open milume on AnnData with spatial coordinates (ileum demo):
import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
w = ml.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w

  1. Draw a selection in the browser (Select regions). Each edit updates w.selections.

  2. Read the latest selection id and the cell names it covers:

sel_id = w.selections[-1]["id"]
hits = w.get_obs_names(sel_id)  # pd.Index of obs_names
  1. Join to observations by name (not row index):
adata.obs["in_selection"] = adata.obs_names.isin(hits)
adata_sel = adata[hits].copy()
  1. Run downstream code on the subset or the flag. Example summary table:
import pandas as pd

summary = pd.DataFrame(
    {"cell_type": adata.obs.loc[hits, "cell_type"].value_counts()}
)

Use w.get_obs_names("focus") when the focused selection in the UI is the one you want (Methods).

items.title: Result
items.text:
hits and adata_sel (or adata.obs["in_selection"]) stay aligned with the map. Re-run steps 3–5 after you change selections in the widget.

Landmarks (w.landmarks) are durable geometry; selections are analysis regions. Traitlets and edge cases are in the LandmarksWidget API.

items.title: Use with AI agents
items.text:
Install the use-milume skill so your agent knows LandmarksWidget workflows and the public API:

npx skills add ckmah/milume --skill use-milume

In Claude Code:

/plugin marketplace add ckmah/milume
/plugin install use-milume@milume

After pip install milume, copy the skill that matches your installed version (stdlib only, no Node):

python -m milume.skill install

Optional target directory and overwrite:

python -m milume.skill install ./.agents/skills --force

items.title: Recipes
items.text:
Each recipe is one marimo notebook under demos/recipes/. The docs site serves a prepared studio export (fixed widget state). Draw new selections or re-run analysis in molab.

Needs the same optional packages as the demos (squidpy, scanpy, leidenalg where noted). 2D recipes use the ileum tier via milume.datasets.ileum_merfish_xu2026() (#380).

items.title: Changelog
items.text:
What changed in each milume release, newest first. Dates are the day the release reached PyPI (Pacific time). Each section links to its GitHub release for the full list of pull requests.

To check which version you have:

import milume
milume.__version__

items.title: Unreleased
items.text:
Not on PyPI yet

Version 2.1.0 is on the release branch. pip install milume still gives 2.0.0 until the release is published.

Genes load on demand, the install is lighter, and docs follow a Diátaxis layout. The public Python API matches 2.0.0. Internal widget traits changed as noted under Changed and Removed.

Added

  • Genes load on demand with an 8-gene picker (Mean, Median, or Max when four or more genes are active). See Color & layers.
  • The use-milume skill installs with npx skills add ckmah/milume --skill use-milume or python -m milume.skill install.

Fixed

  • The Inspect (I) shortcut works when the pointer is over the map.
  • molab demos tell you to click Run all.
  • Vertex-only lasso selections show Measure category counts.
  • Escape in the gene picker only closes the popup.
  • Python 3.14 installs no longer fail on an ancient s3fs build.

Changed

  • pip install milume no longer installs matplotlib, polars, or leidenalg. Install them yourself when your notebooks or recipes need them.
  • Dependency floors for spatialdata, pyarrow, and s3fs; a smaller sdist; a minified widget bundle; and a brighter default Inspect contrast limit.
  • If your code read w.gene_columns, use w.gene_names instead.

Removed

  • The milume[demo] extra. Use each demo's script header or uv sync --group demo.
  • Internal traits gene_format and gene_values (not part of the public API).

Docs

  • Recipes, tutorials, Datasets, and Concepts pages under the Diátaxis restructure.

items.title: 2.0.0 (October 20, 2026)
items.text:
Coloring and reading cells in a region each have one way to do them now, and the Inspect cube draws cells as 3D meshes. This release breaks code written for 1.3.x with no deprecation period, so read the breaking changes before you upgrade.

Breaking

1.3.x 2.0.0 w.set_color(adata.obs["cell_type"]) w.color = "cell_type" w.set_color(gene_values, legend_title="APOB") w.color = "APOB" w.set_color(values) with a computed array adata.obs["score"] = values, then w.color = "score" w.set_points(x, y, color=..., color_map=..., ...) w.set_points(x, y), then w.color = key w.color_by Removed. Read w.color. w.get_obs_names(adata, sel_id) w.get_obs_names(sel_id) w.get_obs_names() for every cell adata.obs_names w.get_focus_obs_names(adata) w.get_obs_names("focus") w.assign_obs_mask(adata, key, sel_id) adata.obs[key] = adata.obs_names.isin(w.get_obs_names(sel_id)) milume.peek(sdata, labels="cells") milume.peek(sdata, shapes="cell_boundaries_z") w.volume["labels_url"] w.volume["cells"] w.volume_label_ids w.volume_cell_rows
  • An unknown color key raises milume.ColorKeyError. A gene that wasn't loaded, or a category column with more than 128 values, raises milume.ColorValueError. The widget stays as it was when either one raises.
  • w.get_obs_names(region) returns a pd.Index instead of a NumPy array, and raises KeyError for an unknown selection id instead of returning nothing.
  • A hidden selection still returns its cells. Hiding only changes the display.
  • One Esc in Inspect closes the cube and leaves Inspect. It used to take two.
  • Inspect needs a shapes element with per-slice cell polygons (cell_id and Z_um columns) to draw cells. Stores without one, such as Xenium and CosMx, open Inspect with the image only.

New

  • Open, move, and close the Inspect cube from Python:

    w.inspect_cx, w.inspect_cy = 120.0, 140.0  # optional, defaults to the volume center
w.inspect_open = True
w.inspect_cx = 150.0  # moves the cube
w.inspect_open = False

    w.inspect_open also reads True or False when you open or close the cube in the browser. - Inspect draws each cell as a 3D mesh built from the cell polygons. Meshes sit inside the image by depth, so image in front of a cell shows in front of it. - Inspect has a minimap. Click or drag on it to move the cube.

Full 2.0.0 release

items.title: 1.3.5 (October 14, 2026)
items.text:
Lasso and Inspect polish. No API changes.

Fixed

  • A quick lasso drag now makes a selection. It used to count as a click.

Changed

  • Inspect always draws cell outlines, and the Cut outline toggle is gone. From the top, each cell shows as a ring you can see through.

Full 1.3.5 release

items.title: 1.3.4 (October 11, 2026)
items.text:
Lasso works on molab. No API changes.

Fixed

  • On molab, lasso drags draw and make a selection, and page text no longer gets selected while you drag.
  • Inspect cube framing, Save snapshots, and cut outlines on data with uneven voxel spacing.

Full 1.3.4 release

items.title: 1.3.3 (October 11, 2026)
items.text:
More molab fixes. No API changes.

Fixed

  • On molab, selected cells are highlighted on the map and the Inspect cube is centered.
  • Changing the cell or window size no longer resets the zoom.

Full 1.3.3 release

items.title: 1.3.2 (October 10, 2026)
items.text:
Lasso works in marimo, and default sizes follow your data's units. No API changes.

Fixed

  • Lasso selection works in marimo and on molab.
  • The default raster bin and Inspect window sizes come from the µm-per-pixel units in your dataset's metadata. milume falls back to guessing from point spacing only when the metadata has no units.

New

  • With a Z cut or crop, the cut face of the Inspect cube outlines each cell.

Full 1.3.2 release

items.title: 1.3.1 (October 10, 2026)
items.text:
Inspect works on remote kernels such as molab and JupyterHub.

Fixed

  • Inspect images load on remote kernels. Panning in Inspect is also much faster on large stores.
  • In marimo, the Inspect cube no longer fails with "Unexpected end of JSON input".
  • A partial cut survives closing the cube, moving the map, and opening it again.
  • A landmark's color in the panel matches its outline on the map.

Changed

  • pip install milume always installs spatialdata. Platform readers such as spatialdata-io stay optional.

Full 1.3.1 release

items.title: 1.3.0 (October 9, 2026)
items.text:
Xenium and CosMx support, a docs site, and a much richer Inspect cube.

New

  • Load Xenium and CosMx data through spatialdata-io. For CosMx, pass spatial_key="global".
  • A docs site with an API reference and llms.txt for coding agents.
  • Inspect shows cells as points, colors by gene expression, and cuts cross sections. It picks contrast limits from the image and shows labels by default.
  • Select several category groups within one selection set.
  • Loading and error indicators on the map and in Inspect.

Fixed

  • Moving the Inspect window no longer flashes, and toggling neighbors is much faster.

Full 1.3.0 release

items.title: 1.2.0 (October 4, 2026)
items.text:
A reworked Inspect view, and smoother zoom on large sections.

Changed

  • The Inspect cube opens when you release the mouse and fills the plot area.
  • New selections are named after their top category and cell count, such as Epithelial · 214, instead of selection 1. Code that typed an old id literally needs the new name. Read ids from w.selections.
  • Labels draw as outlined shells instead of filled cells. Default label opacity is 0.6.

New

  • Shift+drag, or the Move tool, pans the Inspect window. Python sees the new position in w.inspect_cx and w.inspect_cy.
  • Choose Additive or MIP projection separately for the image and the labels.
  • Windows you keep with Save appear in the Selections list with a thumbnail. Hover any selection row to see its cell count, bounds, and top categories.

Fixed

  • Zoom no longer stalls at the start of a gesture on large sections. Hovering a cell no longer shows a tooltip.
  • Collapsed side panels no longer block page scrolling.

Changes since 1.1.0

items.title: 1.1.0 (September 30, 2026)
items.text:
The first release under the name milume, formerly spatial-rx. The 3D cube now lives inside the Landmarks widget as the Inspect tool.

Breaking

spatial-rx 1.0.x milume 1.1.0 pip install spatial-rx pip install milume import spatial_rx import milume VolumeCubeWidget(...) milume.peek(sdata), then the Inspect tool GalleryWidget Removed

New

  • milume.peek(data) opens a LandmarksWidget for an AnnData or SpatialData object.
  • LandmarksWidget(sdata) finds the table, labels, and 3D image in your SpatialData and opens them in the Inspect cube.
  • Inspect shows a live preview under the cursor and loads the docked cube at full resolution. It uses about a third of the memory it did before.
  • Save in the cube's title bar keeps the current window as an inspect selection.
  • milume.enrichment and milume.nearest_distances join the measure functions. With 3D coordinates, distances, along_positions, and composition also report depth, binned by z_bin_size (1 µm by default).

Changes since spatial-rx 1.0.1

Fields: Sub-megabyte committed fixtures under tests/data/ (xenium_ovary_subsample/, cosmx_synthetic_tiny/) plus the Hugging Face xsmall/ tree (100 µm cube cropped from small/; 187 cells kept whole with segmentation and counts).

items.title: 2D
items.text:
Fields: AnnData with authors' log-normalized X (float32 CSR), layers['raw_counts'] (int32 CSR), obsm["spatial"] (µm), obs columns cell_type, cell_class, anatomical_layer, mucosal_pseudospace, and uns["cell_type_colors"]. 1,815 QC-pass genes for the slice (nnz 920,437; median 26 genes/cell and 48 raw counts/cell over those genes). Source obs['n_counts'] median 54 refers to the full panel, not this gene subset.

Load: import milume as ml then ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026() or ml.datasets.ileum_merfish_xu2026() (ml.ds is the same module as ml.datasets). Downloads go to the user cache when the in-repo file is absent. From a checkout you can pass path="demos/data/ileum.h5ad". Registry metadata matches ml.datasets.info("ileum_merfish_xu2026") (Datasets API). Then milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type", genes=[...]) with a short preload list in notebooks so exports stay under the static payload budget; omit genes or pass genes=None to rely on on-demand loading for all 1,815 names. Do not re-normalize: X is already log-normalized.

Citation:

  • Xu RJ, Zhang H, Cadinu P, Nicol PB, Herrmann US, Lee T, Geistlinger L, Irizarry RA, Moffitt JR. Cell Host & Microbe 34(3):509–525.e13 (2026). doi:10.1016/j.chom.2026.01.018

items.title: Datasets
items.text:
Load milume demo AnnData from pip or molab without a git checkout (#380).

import milume as ml

adata = ml.ds.ileum_merfish_xu2026()
names = ml.datasets.list_datasets()
meta = ml.datasets.info("ileum_merfish_xu2026")
path = ml.datasets.fetch("ileum_merfish_xu2026")

ml.ds is an alias for the same module object as ml.datasets (ml.ds is ml.datasets). Use either name after import milume as ml.

Downloads use stdlib urllib, stream to a .part file, verify a pinned sha256, then rename into place. The cache root is $MILUME_DATA_DIR, then $XDG_CACHE_HOME/milume, then ~/.cache/milume. URLs are pinned to an immutable git ref (never main).

items.title: LandmarksWidget API
items.text: Reference for milume.peek and the synced widget handle it returns. For a walkthrough, see Quickstart.

items.title: milume.peek
items.text:
Open a Milume surface on AnnData or SpatialData. This is the main notebook entry point; it constructs LandmarksWidget with the same keyword arguments.

import milume

w = milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
w = milume.peek(sdata)  # table, cell polygons, image inferred

Returns a LandmarksWidget handle. Synced traitlets include w.selections and w.landmarks; join to adata with get_obs_names(region).

items.title: Parameters
items.text:
• data, adata — AnnData with spatial coordinates, or SpatialData (volume inferred). milume.peek names this argument data; LandmarksWidget names the same argument adata.
  • spatial_key — obsm key for x/y coordinates (default "spatial").
  • color — obs column or var_names gene for point colour. When omitted, the first detected categorical column is used. Assign w.color = key later to recolour; unknown keys raise before anything changes.
  • genes — Genes offered for view-only colouring. None (default) offers every var_name and sends each gene's values only when it is first coloured. A name or list restricts the catalog and preloads it when it packs under 64 MiB; larger lists load on demand too, with a warning.
  • table, image, shapes — SpatialData-only overrides for the inferred table, multiscale image, and the shapes element of per-slice cell polygons (cell_id and Z_um columns) the Inspect cube meshes. False leaves one out.
  • channels — SpatialData-only channel names to show on open (e.g. ["DAPI"]). Unknown names raise ValueError listing the available names. For 3D images only one channel is allowed in this version.
  • contrast_limits — SpatialData-only image contrast (min, max) for the Inspect cube. Defaults to the coarsest pyramid level's 1st percentile and max.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
The widget keeps a reference to adata (no obs.copy(), no full-X densify at construct). Chrome follows the notebook cell width; height starts at 720px and is resizable. point_size is the marker radius in the same units as obsm x/y (not a visibility flag). It is seeded at 0.4 times the median nearest-neighbor distance. _cells_visible hides the dots and restores that same radius. When a micrometre scale is known (_um_per_unit, from a SpatialData coordinate system in micrometres, an AnnData uns['spatial'] scale factor, or uns['spatial_units']), the Layers slider edits dot diameter from 1 to 50 µm and the seeded radius is clamped into that range. With no scale, point_size stays in raw coordinate units and the slider labels them px. Neighbourhood expand runs in the browser from coordinates; no obsp graphs are required.

UI chrome (mode, neighbourhoods, raster controls) stays in the browser and is not part of the notebook API. Raster bins and probe scores are built client-side from the loaded gene, embedding, and category packs.

items.title: Synced traitlets
items.text:
Public traitlets from the registry (milume.landmarks._PUBLIC_TRAITS). Other synced fields are internal plumbing and may change without notice.

Name Type Default Meaning color str list[str] "" selections List[Dict] [] Drawn selections as dicts with id, name, geometry and point indices. landmarks List[Dict] [] Drawn landmarks (points, lines, splines, shapes) as dicts. selected_kind str "" Kind of the focused item: selection, landmark, type, or empty. selected_index int -1 Index of the focused item within its kind, or -1. selected_type_indices List[Int] [] Focused category label indices when selected_kind is type. inspect_cx float None Inspect window centre x in spatial units, or None before placement; set it to move the window and the open cube. inspect_cy float None Inspect window centre y in spatial units, or None before placement; set it to move the window and the open cube. inspect_size_um float 300.0 Inspect window side length in µm. inspect_open bool False Whether the Inspect cube is open; True opens it at inspect_cx/cy, or at the volume centre when no window is placed; False closes it and exits Inspect. ValueError without a 3D image. volume dict — The 3D image behind the Inspect cube (image path, cell polygons path and size, voxel size, origin, contrast); {} without one. Read it, don't set it. volume_cut List[Float] [] Cube cut box [x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1] in µm; the browser writes it on slider release, assign it to cut from Python. active_category str "" Deprecated: derived from color; removed in 3.0. active_genes List[Unicode] [] Deprecated: derived from color; removed in 3.0.

items.title: GeoDataFrame interchange
items.text:
Convert w.landmarks to a durable GeoPandas table (and back). Control vertices live in a JSON vertices column; geometry is a GIS proxy. The widget does not own SpatialData — assign sdata['landmarks'] = gdf in the notebook if needed.

Requires optional geopandas and shapely.

items.title: landmarks_to_geodataframe()
items.text:
def landmarks_to_geodataframe(landmarks: list[dict] | None)

Convert widget landmark dicts to a GeoDataFrame.

items.title: Parameters
items.text: • landmarks — Landmark dicts from w.landmarks, or None / [] for an empty frame with contract columns (id, type, vertices, …).

items.title: Returns
items.text: • geopandas.GeoDataFrame — Proxy geometry plus JSON vertices as the round-trip source of truth. Callers assign into SpatialData themselves (e.g. sdata["landmarks"] = gdf).

items.title: Examples
items.text:
import milume
w = milume.peek(adata)
gdf = milume.landmarks_to_geodataframe(w.landmarks)
len(gdf)
0

items.title: geodataframe_to_landmarks()
items.text:
def geodataframe_to_landmarks(gdf)

Convert a landmarks GeoDataFrame back to widget dicts.

items.title: Parameters
items.text: • gdf — GeoDataFrame produced by landmarks_to_geodataframe, or None / zero rows.

items.title: Returns
items.text: • list[dict] — Widget landmark dicts suitable for w.landmarks = .... Empty input yields [].

items.title: Examples
items.text:
import milume
w = milume.peek(adata)
w.landmarks = milume.geodataframe_to_landmarks(
... milume.landmarks_to_geodataframe(w.landmarks) ... )

Label -> hex colour of a categorical column, as the map draws it.

Defaults to the active category. Use it to colour other views (plots, the cube) the same way as the points.

items.text:

items.title: select_type()
items.text:
def select_type(index: int) -> None

Focus one category group in the active set (replaces a multi-select union).

The browser may set selected_type_indices to several groups; this helper is the notebook path for single-group focus without fighting front-end sync.

items.title: get_obs_names()
items.text:
def get_obs_names(region: str) -> 'pd.Index'

obs_names of the cells in region as a pd.Index.

region is a selection id from w.selections, or "focus" for the focused selection or category groups (empty when nothing is focused). A hidden selection still returns its cells; hiding only affects display. Raises KeyError for an unknown id. Write a column with adata.obs[key] = adata.obs_names.isin(w.get_obs_names(region)).

items.title: set_points()
items.text:
def set_points(x: Any, y: Any) -> None

Move the scatter points; colour stays on color.

items.title: set_expression()
items.text:
def set_expression(expr: Any) -> None

Replace the gene catalog from a table (view-only).

Every column becomes a gene; it preloads under the eager size limit and loads on demand above it, like genes=.

items.title: set_render_mode()
items.text:
def set_render_mode(mode: str) -> None

Switch canvas between point scatter and spatial raster bins.

items.text:
def set_raster_basis(*, genes: str | None = None, embedding: str | None = None, composition: str | None = None) -> None

Select bin aggregation basis (genes / embedding / composition).

Bin feature matrices are built in the browser; this only updates traits.

items.title: clear_raster_query()
items.text:
def clear_raster_query() -> None

Clear the pinned similarity query bin.

items.title: Measure
items.text: Quantify landmarks and selections in Python. Every function returns a tidy pandas.DataFrame with one row per cell (or per group).

items.title: Setup
items.text:
Draw a landmark (for example a spline, key 3) and a selection, then build a GeoDataFrame from the widget (needs geopandas):

import milume
from milume import landmarks_to_geodataframe
w = milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type")
gdf = landmarks_to_geodataframe(w.landmarks)
sel = w.get_obs_names(w.selections[-1]["id"])

obs_key names the obs column to group cells by; every output has a group column with its values. When obsm["spatial"] has x, y and z, the outputs also carry z and z_bin (1 µm bins by default, z_bin_size=None turns them off).

items.title: distances
items.text:
distances(adata, landmarks, *, obs_key, spatial_key="spatial", obs_names=None, z_bin_size=1.0)

Per-cell distance to each landmark's geometry. A line or spline with a buffer only measures cells inside the buffer.

from milume import distances
d = distances(adata, gdf, obs_key="cell_type")
d[["obs_name", "landmark_id", "group", "distance"]]

items.title: composition
items.text:
composition(adata, landmarks, *, obs_key, spatial_key="spatial", obs_names=None, z_bin_size=1.0)

Counts and proportions of each group inside a shape or a line's buffer.

from milume import composition
c = composition(adata, gdf, obs_key="cell_type")
c.groupby("group")["count"].sum()

items.title: along_positions
items.text:
along_positions(adata, landmarks, *, obs_key, spatial_key="spatial", obs_names=None, radius=None, z_bin_size=1.0)

Projects cells onto a line or spline as a normalized arc position s from 0 (start) to 1 (end).

from milume import along_positions
s = along_positions(adata, gdf, obs_key="cell_type")
s[["obs_name", "group", "s", "distance"]]

items.title: enrichment
items.text:
enrichment(adata, obs_names, *, obs_key, background=None)

Group composition of a cell subset (such as a selection) against a background, all cells by default.

from milume import enrichment
e = enrichment(adata, sel, obs_key="cell_type")
e[["group", "count", "proportion", "background_proportion", "log2_enrichment"]]

items.title: nearest_distances
items.text:
nearest_distances(adata, seeds, *, obs_key, spatial_key="spatial", obs_names=None)

Distance from every cell to its nearest seed cell, in XY and in XYZ. Needs x, y, z in obsm["spatial"].

from milume import nearest_distances
n = nearest_distances(adata, sel, obs_key="cell_type")
n[["obs_name", "group", "seed", "distance_xy", "distance_xyz"]]

items.title: write_obs
items.text:
write_obs(adata, df, column, value_col, *, obs_name_col="obs_name")

Writes a per-cell measurement back into adata.obs, aligned by obs_name. Cells missing from df stay NaN.

from milume import write_obs
write_obs(adata, d, "dist_to_landmark", "distance")
adata.obs["dist_to_landmark"].describe()

The new column works like any other obs column, for example in scanpy plots or as input to the next peek.

items.title: peek()
items.text:
Open LandmarksWidget on AnnData or SpatialData.

Full signature, parameters, and behaviour are documented in the LandmarksWidget API (peek() section).

items.title: Widget UI
items.text:
Every tool and mode in the milume widget, with its icon and keyboard shortcut. See Keyboard shortcuts for global keys.

1 Navigate VSelect, pan, zoom, minimap, rulers, full screen. 2 Select regions LLasso, Square, Circle and Shape regions you read back in Python. 3 Landmarks 1–4Points, lines, splines and shapes with buffers. 4 Color & layersColor by category, gene or embedding; points or raster; the layers list. 5 Inspect in 3D IA 3D cube of image, labels and transcripts you can slice and orbit. 6 Probe PHover or pin a bin to see raster similarity. MeasureDistances, composition and enrichment from Python.

Start with milume.peek(...): see Load AnnData / SpatialData.

items.title: Color & layers
items.text:
Switch the color panel between category, genes and embed; the map recolors to match.

import milume
w = milume.peek(adata, color="cell_type", genes=["GeneA", "GeneB", "GeneC"])
w.color  # obs column, gene, gene list, or obsm key (e.g. "X_pca")

items.title: Color tabs
items.text:
The right panel has three pill tabs. They have no icons, so the table names each tab.

Tab What it colors by 1 category An obs category column. Expand it () to toggle single subcategories. 2 genes Expression of the picked genes, with ridgeline densities and a blend legend. Pick genes in the field under the legend. 3 embed An embedding (for example X_pca) mapped to RGB, with an RGB-cube legend. Choose the embedding from the dropdown.

items.title: genes
items.text:
Pick up to three genes to blend them, one colour channel each. Pick four to eight and the cells colour by one combined value on a single ramp; choose Mean, Median or Max of the picked genes' normalized expression under the gene field.

Each gene's values load from the kernel the first time you colour by it, so the widget opens fast on whole-transcriptome panels (an 18k-gene Atera breast section included). genes=[...] preloads a short list instead, which helps when the kernel is slow to reply. A list that would pack over 64 MiB loads on demand too, with a warning.

items.title: Points ⇄ Raster
items.text: Control What it does points/raster Flip between drawing each cell as a point and aggregating cells into raster bins (). The icon shows the current mode.

items.title: Layers list
items.text:
The left panel lists every selection and landmark.

Control What it does 1 Selections Click a row to make that selection active. 2 Landmarks Click a row to select the landmark and open its context toolbar. Layer actions Hide / Show, Rename, Delete. Collapse left panel ([) Hide the list; see Navigate.

See Methods for set_color, set_raster_basis and the rest.

items.title: Inspect in 3D
items.text:
Place a cube window on the map, then orbit and slice image, labels and transcripts together.

import milume
w = milume.peek(sdata, image="mosaic", shapes="cell_boundaries_z")  # press I, then click the tissue
w.volume_cut  # cut-plane state after you slide the cross-section

items.title: Entering Inspect
items.text: Press I or click Inspect, then click the tissue to place a cube window. The top pill shows the window size, Save window and Exit Inspect (Esc).

items.title: Inspect toolbar
items.text: Control What it does 1 Top / Iso / Side Snap the camera to a top, oblique or side view. 2 Move Drag to pan the cube window on the map. Reset view Return the cube camera to its default. 3 Image Show or hide the image layer. Right-click for palette, contrast, alpha, gamma and projection. 4 Labels Show or hide the cell meshes. Right-click for their opacity. 5 Points Show or hide the points layer. Cross-section Slide a cut plane through the cube.

items.title: Cross-section
items.text:
See Synced traitlets for Inspect fields, and Constructor parameters for image= / shapes= on milume.peek. With several 3D images, pass image= to pick one. Stores without per-slice cell polygons (e.g. Xenium / CosMx) open Inspect image-only, with no cells; 2D image plus polygon rendering is tracked in #122.

Cell meshes run in an inline Web Worker. Strict notebook Content-Security-Policies must allow worker-src blob: (the defaults in JupyterLab and VS Code already do).

items.title: Landmarks
items.text:
Click to place landmark vertices, press Enter to finish, then widen a buffer around the line.

import milume
w = milume.peek(adata)  # press 3, click points, Enter
w.landmarks             # list of landmark dicts

Landmarks are durable geometric annotations (points, lines, splines, shapes). Selections are analysis regions; see Select regions.

items.title: Draw tools
items.text:
The four landmark tools share one toolbar button. Click it to arm the last-used tool, or right-click it to pick another.

Control What it does Point (1) Click once to place a point. Line (2) Click vertices of a polyline; press Enter to finish. Spline (3) Click control points of a smooth curve; press Enter to finish. Shape (4) Click vertices of a closed shape; press Enter to finish. Node (N) Drag, insert or delete vertices of the selected landmark.

items.title: Context toolbar
items.text:
Click a landmark with Select (V) to open its toolbar at the bottom of the map.

Control What it does Line style Toggle solid or dashed. 1 Color Six swatches plus a custom color. 2 Tension How tightly a spline follows its control points. 3 Buffer Signed buffer width: negative is left or in, positive is right or out. Both sides makes it symmetric; Reset buffer sets it to 0. 4 Make selection from buffer Turn the cells inside the buffer into a selection. Reverse Flip the direction of a line or spline. 5 Convert type Convert between Line, Spline and Shape.

items.title: Right-click menu
items.text:
Control What it does Hide / Show Toggle the landmark's visibility. Rename Give the landmark a new name. Duplicate Copy the landmark. Delete (⌫) Remove the landmark. Insert node In Node mode, add a vertex where you right-clicked. Delete node (⌫) In Node mode, remove the active vertex.

Export landmarks from Python with Draw and export landmarks. See GeoDataFrame interchange in the API reference.

items.title: Navigate
items.text:
Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, and press 0 to fit the whole tissue back in view.

import milume
w = milume.peek(sdata)  # press H to pan, = / - to zoom, 0 to reset

items.title: Controls
items.text: Control What it does Select (V) Default tool. Click a selection or landmark to open its context toolbar. Move (H) Drag anywhere to pan. Hold Space to pan with any tool. Zoom in (=) Zoom in one step. The scroll wheel also zooms. Zoom out (-) Zoom out one step. Reset view (0) Fit all cells in view. Canvas rulers Show coordinate rulers along the top and left edges. Full screen (F) Fill the screen with the widget;  Exit full screen returns. Collapse left / right panel ([ / ]) Hide a side panel;  Show left panel brings it back. Minimap Drag the viewport box to pan; scroll on it to zoom.

items.title: Canvas rulers
items.text: For keyboard shortcuts see Keyboard shortcuts. To drive the active tool from Python, see Synced traitlets.

items.title: Probe
items.text:
Hover a bin with Probe on; similar bins light up. Click to pin the query.

Probe compares raster bins, so switch the map to raster first ( points/raster; see Color & layers).

import milume
w = milume.peek(adata, genes=["GeneA", "GeneB", "GeneC"])
w.set_render_mode("raster")  # then press P and hover

items.title: Controls
items.text:
Control What it does Probe (P) Hover a bin to color every bin by its similarity to it; click to pin that bin. Similarity legend Color scale from 0 (dissimilar) to 1 (identical), shown in the right panel while Probe is on. Esc Clear the probe.

With the genes tab active, similarity uses the picked genes; pick at least one gene first, or hovering does nothing.

items.title: Select regions
items.text:
Draw a lasso, square, circle or shape around cells, then read the selection back in Python.

import milume
w = milume.peek(adata)  # press L, then drag around some cells
sel_id = w.selections[-1]["id"]

items.title: Controls
items.text:
The four selection tools share one toolbar button. Click it to arm the last-used tool, or right-click it to pick another.

Control What it does Lasso (L) Drag a freehand outline. Square (R) Drag a rectangle. Circle (O) Drag an ellipse. Shape (G) Click vertices of a polygon; press Enter to finish. Shape menu (right-click) Choose which of the four tools the button arms. Layer actions Rename, hide or delete the selection from the layers list.

items.title: While a selection is active
items.text:
The cells inside stay at full color and the right panel counts only them. A small toolbar at the bottom of the map offers Radius neighborhood and k-NN neighborhood around the selection, with Make selection to keep that neighborhood as a new selection. Press ⌫ or Delete to remove the active selection.

Read selections in Python with Use selections downstream. See Methods for the full signatures.
